split-01.title: Your Speedflip Is Outdated
split-01.description: The coach pulls up film: your speedflip kickoff loses 50/50s against every top team. Rebuilding muscle memory mid-split is risky, but the flaw is costing goals.

a.label: Rebuild the kickoff from scratch in free play
a.outcome: A week in free play and the flip finally lands. Kickoff 50s start going your way. Your hands are wrecked.
a.failure: You tear the kickoff down and can't put it back. For days you lose every 50 you used to win on instinct.

b.label: Keep the old kickoff until the offseason
b.outcome: You keep the old flip. The 50s stay a problem, but at least you still have a kickoff you trust.
b.failure: You stick with it and get punished anyway. Opponents wait on the same tell. Nothing feels safe on kickoff.

c.label: Grind it quietly after scrims every night
c.outcome: Night reps after scrims sharpen the flip. You show up to review looking like you haven't slept.
c.failure: You grind the flip at 1 a.m. and still whiff it in the next scrim. The late nights were for nothing.

split-02.title: The Replay Review Stings
split-02.description: The analyst freezes the frame on two double commits that gifted the series away. Everyone in the room knows it's you on screen.

a.label: Own it and drill rotations until they're automatic
a.outcome: You own the double commits and drill rotations until they're boring. The callout still sits in your chest.
a.failure: You drill rotations all week and still double commit in the next series. The room goes quiet again.

b.label: Defend your reads: the pass was on
b.outcome: You defend the read. The room stays tense. You walk out with your head up, and nobody forgot the clip.
b.failure: You argue the pass was on. Teammates stop calling your name in voice. The next block is icy.

c.label: Ask for a full team review instead of a callout
c.outcome: A full team review spreads the blame. Rotations get a rewrite. Everyone leaves sharper, including you.
c.failure: You ask for a team review and it turns into an hour of finger-pointing. Nobody wants to watch film tomorrow.

split-03.title: One Week Before the First Regional
split-03.description: A free week before the split kicks off, and the roster is divided on how to spend it.

a.label: Solo-queue 1v1s ten hours a day
a.outcome: Ten-hour 1v1 blocks. Your mechanics spike. Your hands are cooked, and in team voice you sound like you haven't talked to anyone in days.
a.failure: Ten hours of 1s and you still can't convert. You show up to scrims slower, and the roster noticed you skipped them.

b.label: Lock in a full scrim block against contenders
b.outcome: A full scrim week against contenders. Kickoffs, shadows, and mid-field passes start to feel like one idea.
b.failure: You book the contender block and get farmed. Confidence leaks into the regional week.

c.label: Take real rest days and recharge
c.outcome: Real rest days. You show up fresh. A little less hungry, but you can actually see the ball.
c.failure: You take the days off and come back rusty. The first scrim back is a mess of mistimed jumps.

split-04.title: A Sponsor Wants You Streaming
split-04.description: An energy-drink brand offers a deal: four stream nights a week, great money, great for the fans, and it eats straight into training hours.

a.label: Sign it: the community and the paycheck matter
a.outcome: Four stream nights. Chat learns your name. Your ranked hours shrink to whatever's left after the raid.
a.failure: You sign and the streams flop. You still lose the training nights, and the brand starts asking why the average viewership is a joke.

b.label: Turn it down until the season ends
b.outcome: You turn the deal down until the split ends. The sticks stay the priority. The brand will still be there.
b.failure: You decline, then spend the week wondering if you should have taken it. Distracted ranked is still ranked.

split-05.title: The Meta Just Shifted
split-05.description: Top teams now slow-play possession and starve boost. Your fast-paced style suddenly looks punishable.

a.label: Relearn your game around the new meta
a.outcome: You sit in the slow-play. Challenges wait a beat longer. The old demo-hungry you is gone, on purpose.
a.failure: You try to play patient and just… stop challenging. You get scored on from half-field because nobody rotates into the space you left.

b.label: Trust your fundamentals and sharpen what already works
b.outcome: You keep your pace and clean up the sloppy challenges. Some teams hate it. Some teams can't live with it.
b.failure: You double down on speed and get farmed by the possession teams. Every overcommit is on the VOD now.

split-06.title: Your Teammate Is Tilting
split-06.description: After two lost scrim blocks, your teammate is whiffing on purpose and flaming in voice. The first regional is days away.

a.label: Call a team meeting and clear the air
a.outcome: The meeting is ugly, then quiet. Voice is usable again. You spent a night on people instead of packs.
a.failure: The meeting explodes. They mute you for the rest of the night. Regional week starts with a group chat on read.

b.label: Mute comms and grind your own replays
b.outcome: You mute comms and grind your VODs. Your mechanics hold. Nobody is talking in the server.
b.failure: You mute them and they notice. The next scrim is three people playing 1s in the same lobby.

split-07.title: Coach Wants a New System
split-07.description: The coach wants you playing second man instead of your natural first-man style. The data says it wins games; your gut disagrees.

a.label: Full buy-in: run the new rotation all split
a.outcome: You play second man all week. Last-back saves start landing. You miss the ball on your stick.
a.failure: You buy in and freeze. First man goes, you hesitate, and the backboard is empty. The old rotation is gone too.

b.label: Meet halfway: new system in scrims, instincts on stage
b.outcome: New rotations in scrims, your game on stage. It's messy. It also means you still have a first-man when it counts.
b.failure: You mix systems and nobody knows who's last back. The coach stops calling plays mid-series.

c.label: Refuse: you got here playing your way
c.outcome: You refuse the change. Kickoffs stay yours. The coach files it, and the analyst's spreadsheet stays red.
c.failure: You refuse, then get exposed on the same overcommit the data flagged. Nobody says 'I told you so.' They don't have to.

split-08.title: Your Controller Is Giving Out
split-08.description: Stick drift, mid-split. A new controller means re-tuning deadzones and aerial sensitivity days before a regional.

a.label: Swap now and re-tune everything
a.outcome: New controller. Deadzones feel alien for two days, then the aerials start sticking again.
a.failure: You swap and spend the regional hunting a deadzone that never feels like home. Easy shots dump.

b.label: Nurse it through the split with tape and prayers
b.outcome: Tape on the stick. You know the drift. Every aerial is a coin flip you think you can still call.
b.failure: The drift spikes mid-series. You steer into the ceiling on a kickoff you have hit a thousand times.

split-09.title: Freestyle Invitational
split-09.description: A famous freestyler invites you to a clips session that would pull huge views. Your coach wants you drilling shadow defense instead.

a.label: Film the clips: let your name grow
a.outcome: The session pops off. Your name is on the thumbnail. Shadow defense is a problem for tomorrow.
a.failure: You show up for clips and brick every reset on stream. The comments are not about the setup.

b.label: Skip it and drill defense
b.outcome: You skip the invite and drill shadows. Quiet night. The next series, you're actually last back.
b.failure: You skip the session and still check the VOD of who replaced you. The defense block is a write-off.

split-10.title: Bootcamp Abroad
split-10.description: The org offers a three-week bootcamp in another region: elite scrims, zero distractions, and zero home comfort.

a.label: Pack your bags and grind
a.outcome: Three weeks abroad, elite scrims, hotel Wi-Fi. You come back sharper and a little homesick.
a.failure: The bootcamp is a wash. Jet lag, bad ping in the first week, and you never catch the scrim level.

b.label: Stay home and keep your routine
b.outcome: You keep your bed, your monitor, your hours. The reps are familiar. You didn't get the other region's reads.
b.failure: You stay home and the routine goes stale. Same lobby, same mistakes, nobody new to punish you.

split-11.title: The Data Says Otherwise
split-11.description: The analyst's numbers show you challenge too early and burn boost on defense. Fixing your reads means weeks of discomfort.

a.label: Trust the data and rework your challenges
a.outcome: You wait a beat longer. Boost lasts. You miss the old panic challenge more than you'll admit.
a.failure: You try to wait and just… don't challenge. Balls bounce in from mid because you second-guessed a 50 you had.

b.label: Trust your instincts: stats don't see everything
b.outcome: You trust the read in your hands. Some of those early challenges still win games. The spreadsheet stays mad.
b.failure: You ignore the sheet and get caught on the same overcommit, twice, in the same series.

split-12.title: Social Media Storm
split-12.description: After a group-stage exit, a clip of your open-net whiff goes viral. Your mentions are unbearable.

a.label: Log off until the major
a.outcome: You delete the apps until the major. The clip dies. So does the noise that used to keep you sharp.
a.failure: You log off and still hear about it in team voice. Someone sent the clip in the group chat 'as a joke.'

b.label: Post a self-deprecating meme and own it
b.outcome: The meme lands. Chat quotes it for a day. The next series still has to answer the whiff.
b.failure: You post the meme and the replies are worse. Quote-tweets of the original clip, with your joke under it.

c.label: Say nothing and let the next games answer
c.outcome: You say nothing. Queue, scrim, sleep. The next series is the only reply that counts.
c.failure: You stay silent and the clip keeps circulating. In the next opener you're thinking about Twitter, not kickoff.

split-13.title: Add Demos to Your Game?
split-13.description: The coach suggests aggressive demos and bumps on kickoff follow-ups. It wins boost fights but invites chaos, and makes enemies.

a.label: Go full bump mode
a.outcome: You live on the bump. Kickoff fights swing. You also eat a demo you didn't see, every other game.
a.failure: You go bump-hungry and whiff the demo, then the ball. Chaos without the payoff.

b.label: Keep it clean and positional
b.outcome: You stay clean and positional. Boost is still there. Nobody is hunting you off kickoff either.
b.failure: You stay clean and get walked through. The other first man bumps you for free and takes the pad.

split-14.title: Night Owl Problem
split-14.description: Your best mechanics show up at 2 a.m., but team scrims run at noon. Something has to give.

a.label: Fix your sleep schedule around the team's hours
a.outcome: You flip to the team's clock. Noon scrims feel like games. The 2 a.m. peak is gone.
a.failure: You force the sleep schedule and show up groggy anyway. Worst of both clocks.

b.label: Keep grinding nights where you peak
b.outcome: You keep the 2 a.m. packs. Mechanics stay nasty. You look like a ghost in the noon block.
b.failure: You grind nights and still brick in both lobbies. The noon scrims are a write-off and so is your sleep.

split-15.title: Charity Showmatch
split-15.description: You're invited to a charity showmatch with community legends the weekend before a regional. Great vibes, zero prep value.

a.label: Play it: the community gave you everything
a.outcome: You play the showmatch. The donation ticker goes stupid. Your regional warm-up is a lobby with casters yelling memes.
a.failure: You play it, drop every aerial on the broadcast, and still lose Saturday to prep you didn't do.

b.label: Politely decline and scrim instead
b.outcome: You decline and scrim. Cold text to the organizer. The regional block is actually a block.
b.failure: You decline, then watch the showmatch on stream instead of scrimming. You got neither the goodwill nor the reps.

split-16.title: Patch Day
split-16.description: A surprise patch tweaks boost pad respawns and kickoff spawn angles. Every team in the world is relearning the same details tonight.

a.label: Lab the new timings until they're second nature
a.outcome: You lab pads until the new timer is in your hands. Kickoff paths change. You skip a night of sleep to get there.
a.failure: You lab the patch and grout the old timing into the new pads. Double-pads you used to hit are now air.

b.label: Adapt on the fly: feel over theory
b.outcome: You queue and feel it out. Some pads surprise you. You don't lose a whole night to a spreadsheet.
b.failure: You 'feel it out' and get beat to every pad in the next series. The other team labbed.

split-17.title: 1v1 For Content
split-17.description: A big streamer DMs you: 1v1 the new 16-year-old prodigy on stream tonight. Last collab did huge numbers. Your coach has a scrim block at the same hour.

a.label: Play the 1v1. The clip will live forever
a.outcome: BO7 on stream. Chat is feral. You get the thumbnail. You miss the scrims, and the prodigy is now in your head.
a.failure: You get cooked on stream. Open-net in OT, their reset, your whiff. The clip is you. The scrims happened without you.

b.label: Pass. Scrims first
b.outcome: You pass. The streamer books someone else. Your night is three maps of shadow defense with the roster.
b.failure: You skip it and still check the VOD between games. Teammates notice you're half in the scrim.

split-18.title: They Tagged You
split-18.description: A rival posts your worst clip of the split with a caption that isn't even a joke. It's personal. Your mentions are a dumpster fire.

a.label: Quote-tweet them. Don't let it sit
a.outcome: You quote-tweet them. The timeline loves the fight. In scrims you're still composing the next reply.
a.failure: You reply. They post a worse clip. Your coach mutes the Discord until you log off.

b.label: Mute the word and queue
b.outcome: You mute the account, queue ranked, and let the next regional answer. The clip is still out there. You're not.
b.failure: You mute them and still refresh the thread. The next scrim block is you playing with one eye on your phone.

c.label: Let the org post. Stay out of it
c.outcome: The org drops a comeback montage. You stay out of the replies. The clip war is someone else's shift.
c.failure: The org posts a corporate 'we focus on the game' tweet. It reads like a concession. The replies get meaner.

split-19.title: One More Pack
split-19.description: You're in a groove at 1 a.m. Custom training, then ranked, then another pack. The first regional is in four days. The org already asked you to sleep.

a.label: Keep grinding nights until it clicks
a.outcome: You grind until the sun comes up. The mechanics are there. So is the crash: the org sits you for the first two regionals and the major.
a.failure: You grind through the week and show up unable to aerial. They sit you for two regionals and scratch you from the major. The packs didn't even stick.

b.label: Close the game. Sleep. Trust the work
b.outcome: You close the game. Two nights of actual sleep. The pack will still be there. So will you, on the server list.
b.failure: You try to sleep and lie there thinking about the pack you didn't finish. You show up groggy anyway.

split-20.title: A Workshop Map With Your Name On It
split-20.description: A map creator in your Discord offers a custom pack built around the mechanic you keep missing — ceiling resets, or that backboard read. A week of their time. You'd owe them a shoutout, and a week of lab.

a.label: Yes. Lab it until the read is automatic
a.outcome: The pack is nasty. A week later the backboard read is just there. You shout them out. Your usual routine is gone.
a.failure: The pack is built for a mechanic you don't have yet. You grind it anyway and grout bad habits into your hands.

b.label: Pass. Stick to the packs you know
b.outcome: You thank them and stay on the packs you already hit. No new quirks. No new ceiling either.
b.failure: You pass. Two weeks later a rival is grinding that same creator's pack on stream — and hitting the read you don't have.

worlds-01.title: Group of Death
worlds-01.description: The Worlds draw lands you against the world No. 1 and the host region's crowd favorite. Your prep week just got heavy.

a.label: Study every opponent frame by frame
a.outcome: You know their kickoff tells. You also haven't seen sunlight. The group of death is in your laptop.
a.failure: You over-scout and freeze on stage. You wait for a pattern that isn't there, and the opener is gone.

b.label: Focus on your own game: let them adapt to you
b.outcome: You scrim your stuff, not theirs. Confidence is up. You will not know their third-man cheat until you see it live.
b.failure: You skip the tape and get cooked by a kickoff they have run in every series this year.

worlds-02.title: Jet Lag at the LAN
worlds-02.description: You land nine time zones from home, three days before your opener. Everyone handles it differently.

a.label: Strict recovery: sleep, food, light sessions
a.outcome: Sleep, food, light sessions. You land in the opener able to track the ball. You didn't soak the arena at midnight.
a.failure: You force the sleep schedule and still feel like 4 a.m. in the opener. Light sessions weren't enough.

b.label: Midnight arena sessions to soak in the stage
b.outcome: Midnight in the arena. The stage starts to feel like a server. The jet lag does not care.
b.failure: You hit the midnight sessions and play the opener on no sleep. The stage is loud. Your jump is late.

worlds-03.title: Main Stage Nerves
worlds-03.description: Ten thousand fans, casters shouting your gamertag. Your hands are shaking in the warm-up room.

a.label: Walk out early and embrace the crowd
a.outcome: You walk out early. The noise hits, then it turns into fuel. Your hands stop shaking when the countdown starts.
a.failure: You walk out early and the crowd eats you. The shake in your hands is worse on the desk.

b.label: Noise-cancelling on, tunnel vision until game time
b.outcome: Headphones on. You don't look up until game 1. The shake settles. You also never see the room you're in.
b.failure: You hide in the headphones and still choke the first kickoff. Tunnel vision didn't hide the countdown.

worlds-04.title: They Scouted You
worlds-04.description: Word gets around: the favorites built their entire gameplan around shutting you down.

a.label: Rework your kickoff plays overnight
a.outcome: Overnight kickoff rework. They taped the old you. This one fake-challenges on the spawn they always overcommit.
a.failure: You rework kickoffs at 4 a.m. and brick the new setup on stage. They still have the old tape, and now this too.

b.label: Take it as a compliment and double down on your style
b.outcome: You play your game louder. Compliment accepted. If they built a plan around you, make them use it.
b.failure: You double down and run straight into the trap they built. Every challenge is where they wanted it.

worlds-05.title: Media Day Marathon
worlds-05.description: Interviews, photoshoots, broadcast content. It's a full day off the sticks right before the bracket.

a.label: Give the full press run: the fans love it
a.outcome: Full press run. Clips, photos, a bit that will live on the broadcast. The sticks wait until tonight.
a.failure: You do every interview and go blank on stage the next day. Your hands remember the microphone, not the kickoff.

b.label: Do the minimum and get back to warm-ups
b.outcome: One interview, back to warm-ups. Form holds. The camera crew does not love you.
b.failure: You duck media and still can't focus in warm-ups. The org is annoyed. You're not sharper for it.

worlds-06.title: The Kickoff Gamble
worlds-06.description: The night before the bracket, your coach proposes fake kickoffs to counter the favorites' hyper-aggressive first man. High risk, high reward.

a.label: Run the fakes
a.outcome: You run the fakes. If they bite, it's a free ball. If they don't, you're first man in no-man's-land.
a.failure: You run the fake and they don't bite. You're late to everything. The coach stops calling it after game 1.

b.label: Stick to standard speedflips
b.outcome: Standard speedflips. No chaos. They get the kickoff they practiced against. So do you.
b.failure: You stay standard and they still win every 50. No surprise, no answer.

late-01.title: The Spark Is Gone
late-01.description: Another hotel, another scrim block. You catch yourself staring at the desktop instead of queueing. The org still expects a full split.

a.label: Mute Discord and take real days off
a.outcome: You go quiet. The tank refills a little. The scene feels farther away, and that's the point.
a.failure: You take the days off and come back emptier. The desktop is still there. So is the split.

b.label: Turn the slump into content: ranked on stream
b.outcome: The audience shows up. Ranked is content now. Training time is whatever chat doesn't raid.
b.failure: You stream the slump. Chat farms the whiffs. You still didn't get the reps, and now they're public.

c.label: Sit with the academy stack and run their VODs
c.outcome: You spend the week teaching. Your own mechanics idle. The kids get better, and you remember why this was fun.
c.failure: You review academy VODs and zone out. They don't get better. Neither do you.

late-02.title: The Org Wants You On Camera
late-02.description: Content wants four branded streams a week through the offseason. The coach wants you in the facility. You can't do both.

a.label: Take the stream schedule
a.outcome: Lights, overlay, subs. The facility sees you less. Chat sees you more.
a.failure: You take the streams and the numbers are bad. You're still not in the facility. Nobody's happy.

b.label: Stay in the building and help the next roster
b.outcome: You become the voice in review. Playing time dips. The room actually listens.
b.failure: You stay to help and they don't want the notes. You're in the building with nothing to do.

c.label: Decline both and disappear for a month
c.outcome: Phone on Do Not Disturb. No ranked, no Discord. The silence is the point.
c.failure: You disappear and come back to a roster that already moved on. The month didn't fix the spark.

late-03.title: A Rookie Wants Film
late-03.description: An academy first-year slides into DMs: can you review their VODs? Your own mechanics are slipping and the clock is loud.

a.label: Run the film with them every night
a.outcome: You coach more than you queue. The kid improves. So does the part of you that likes teaching.
a.failure: You run film every night and they don't take a single note. Your ranked time is gone.

b.label: Review on stream and make it a series
b.outcome: VOD review as content. The series hits. Your own ranked time does not.
b.failure: The series flops. You're explaining kickoffs to 40 viewers instead of taking them.

c.label: Pass: you need the hours for yourself, or for nothing
